evidence.exact_quote: - **Canonical persistence:** seglog is the canonical store for Project Plan Package artifacts (see §8).

items.impact: Establishes a single persistence authority and makes filesystem materializations subordinate, preventing path-local state from silently becoming canon.
items.statement: Project Plan Package artifacts are canonical in seglog, while the workspace tree is a regenerable staging, export, and cache surface.
items.title: Seglog owns package persistence

evidence.exact_quote: - Generated media project outputs reference durable local artifacts and hashes.

items.impact: Prevents expiring URLs and secret-bearing provider/session data from being mistaken for durable project outputs.
items.statement: Generated-media packaging requires durable local references and hashes, preserves non-secret provider provenance, discloses expiring URLs, and does not take ownership of provider execution.
items.title: Generated media packaging preserves durable provenance

evidence.exact_quote: - Filesystem export MUST be reconstructible by replaying seglog events keyed by `logical_path`.

items.impact: Different builders can choose different winners for duplicate-path events or recover differently after interrupted materialization, defeating byte-identical reconstruction and trust claims.
items.statement: Replay is keyed by logical_path, but this source does not specify ordering, duplicate/tombstone semantics, atomic replacement, or interrupted-replay recovery when multiple events target the same path.
items.title: Replay conflict semantics are missing

evidence.exact_quote: Plans/Project_Output_Artifacts.md is the SSOT for user-project Project Plan Package outputs staged under .puppet-master/project/**, including artifact paths, sharding rules, seglog canonical persistence, DRY contract-referenced sharded headless graph requirements, and optional non-canonical derived exports.

items.impact: Gives downstream plans one place to resolve artifact paths and sharding rules and blocks duplicated competing canon.
items.statement: The document explicitly owns the Project Plan Package output SSOT and anti-duplication boundary.
items.title: Project output SSOT is explicit

evidence.exact_quote: Project Plan Package artifacts are distinct from GUI Runtime Artifacts; optional runtime-analysis exports are projections of canonical runtime identities, and debug/runtime targets bind to the package only through explicit project/session/runtime identity.

items.impact: Prevents GUI runtime evidence and user-project deliverables from sharing an accidental persistence or identity model.
items.statement: Runtime Artifacts and Project Plan Package artifacts are explicitly separate families, joined only through canonical project/session/runtime identities.
items.title: Runtime and project artifact families stay distinct

evidence.exact_quote: Project artifact events, Auditor cycle reports, and legacy pass-report compatibility mirrors must align to EventRecord-level identity, register missing artifact and event families, and resolve report lineage across project, run, thread, wizard, account, provider, model, and later launched run identity.

items.impact: Blocks downstream export and handoff claims until the upstream report can be traced across every required identity boundary.
items.statement: Artifact events and Auditor report families must carry EventRecord-level lineage across planning, runtime, account, provider, model, and launched-run identities.
items.title: Artifact event identity gates downstream claims

evidence.exact_quote: Artifact opening and navigation must be identity-native, supporting generated and staged artifacts before backing paths exist while preserving project/run-aware resolver metadata for FileManager, Runtime Artifacts, ledger/history/search, and attempt-scoped evidence views.

items.impact: Surfaces may disagree on stale, missing, uncaptured, offline, or degraded artifacts and present an open action that resolves differently by caller.
items.statement: Identity-native opening is required, but resolver precedence, freshness checks, degraded fallback, unavailable-path states, and user-visible failure outcomes are not defined in this unit.
items.title: Identity-native open lacks resolver states

evidence.exact_quote: Exported artifact records preserve canonical IDs and refs, disclose or refresh stale/degraded projection trust, keep compatibility aliases subordinate to canonical identities, preserve stable project identity across moves/rebinds, and keep health, activity, and attention distinct.

items.impact: Prevents exports and GUI summaries from hiding degraded trust or inventing identities that cannot round-trip to canon.
items.statement: Exports preserve canonical IDs, subordinate aliases, stable project identity, and visible stale/degraded trust state.
items.title: Exports retain trust and canonical identity

evidence.exact_quote: Project Plan Package artifacts are canonical in seglog; filesystem materialization under .puppet-master/project/** is staging/export/cache and must be regenerable with byte-identical hash verification.

items.impact: Provides a falsifiable byte-level oracle for staged package reconstruction.
items.statement: Byte-identical hash verification is the acceptance oracle for filesystem regeneration from canonical seglog artifacts.
items.title: Reconstruction has a byte-identity oracle

evidence.exact_quote: Puppet Master must persist the required Project Plan Package artifact set canonically in seglog, with sharded graph paths, required traceability outputs, optional non-canonical quickstart, and a staging tree matching the listed paths.

items.impact: Makes omissions detectable and preserves the authority difference between required artifacts and convenience exports.
items.statement: The package defines a required persisted artifact set, canonical sharded paths, traceability outputs, and an optional noncanonical quickstart.
items.title: Required package output set is enumerated

evidence.exact_quote: If the generated project includes interactive GUI surfaces dispatching UICommand IDs, Puppet Master emits both GUI artifacts; when no interactive GUI surface is in scope, both may be absent.

items.impact: Makes one-file-only GUI wiring output an invalid and testable package state.
items.statement: Interactive GUI projects emit the wiring matrix and UI command catalog as an all-or-none pair.
items.title: GUI artifact trigger is paired

evidence.exact_quote: Execution-time Attempt Journal, Parent Summary, AGENTS, and iteration artifacts live in the non-canonical workspace sidecar, while .puppet-master/project/** remains package staging and .puppet-master/state/** remains reserved for project-local runtime state.

items.impact: Prevents execution journals and runtime state from being promoted into package canon by location alone.
items.statement: Workspace sidecar, project staging, and runtime state occupy distinct non-interchangeable storage domains.
items.title: Execution sidecar is noncanonical

evidence.exact_quote: Markdown/text artifacts under .puppet-master/** that reach packaging triggers become adjacent .docset/ Document Sets per policy, with the original path retained as a deterministic derived pointer stub.

items.impact: A crash or concurrent read during file-to-docset conversion could expose both forms as canonical, neither form as usable, or a pointer to incomplete shards.
items.statement: The target packaged form and pointer stub are defined, but the transition's atomic publication, interruption recovery, and concurrent-reader behavior are delegated or absent here.
items.title: Document Set conversion lacks transition recovery

evidence.exact_quote: Packaged Document Sets make index, manifest, shards, and evidence canonical for the logical artifact while the original path remains only a derived pointer stub; sharded plan graph identity remains unchanged.

items.impact: Prevents unbounded recursive packaging and preserves graph identity through large-document conversion.
items.statement: Document Set members become canonical for the logical artifact, the original becomes a pointer, and generated members cannot recursively trigger packaging.
items.title: Document Set canon and no-recursion rule are explicit

evidence.exact_quote: The listed Puppet Master internal schemas and exact field names are authoritative; this document owns paths, sharding, DRY requirements, and cross-file integrity rules.

items.impact: Rejects implementation-local field renames and makes schema conformance mechanically testable.
items.statement: Internal schema identifiers and field names are authoritative and must remain exact.
items.title: Schema field names are locked

evidence.exact_quote: Internal Platform Contracts are referenced by stable IDs, while generated Project Contracts live in the Project Contract Pack; contracts/index.json is the canonical mapping from ProjectContract:* IDs to kind, path, sha256, and related metadata.

items.impact: Preserves the boundary between Puppet Master internals and generated user-project contracts while providing a canonical resolver.
items.statement: Platform Contracts are stable-ID references, while the generated contract-pack index owns ProjectContract resolution and hashes.
items.title: Platform and project contract layers are separated

evidence.exact_quote: Node shards and acceptance manifests cross-reference Project Contract IDs instead of duplicating specifications, and human plan.md summaries must point to canonical ProjectContract sources.

items.impact: Keeps node, acceptance, and human-plan consumers synchronized with canonical contract text.
items.statement: Graph nodes, acceptance checks, and plan summaries reference canonical ProjectContract identities rather than copying contract prose.
items.title: DRY contract references propagate across outputs

evidence.exact_quote: Puppet Master applies deterministic defaults autonomously, records valid ambiguities to user-project auto_decisions.jsonl, keeps internal SSOT decisions separate, and supports optional HITL approval-boundary nodes through tool_policy_mode: "ask".

items.impact: An unattended or offline run can either stall forever, bypass an approval boundary, or conflict with the separate rule that ambiguity logging is non-gating.
items.statement: The unit combines autonomous continuation with optional tool_policy_mode ask nodes but does not define the runtime transition when an approval-boundary node has no available approver.
items.title: Optional approval boundary lacks unattended behavior

evidence.exact_quote: Puppet Master produces user-project plans as a canonical sharded-only graph under .puppet-master/project/plan_graph/, while plan.md remains the required human-readable view.

items.impact: Separates machine execution authority from the required human-readable projection.
items.statement: The sharded graph is canonical for headless execution and plan.md remains a required human view, not an execution authority.
items.title: Canonical graph and human plan have distinct roles

evidence.exact_quote: The canonical graph entrypoint is always plan_graph/index.json; node files live under nodes/, optional edges.json is allowed, and any monolithic graph is a labeled derived export only.

items.impact: Eliminates ambiguity over which graph representation orchestration and validation may trust.
items.statement: The index is the locked canonical entrypoint; edges are optional and monolithic graphs are derived exports only.
items.title: Plan graph entrypoint is locked

evidence.exact_quote: Node IDs must be stable and reproducible from canonical node intent for identical inputs so shard filenames remain deterministic.

items.impact: Independent compilers can generate different node IDs from semantically identical intent, breaking shard stability, references, merges, and migration compatibility.
items.statement: Stable IDs are required, but this unit does not define the canonical node-intent serialization, normalization, hash/encoding algorithm, collision behavior, or versioning needed for reproducibility.
items.title: Deterministic node ID algorithm is under-specified

evidence.exact_quote: plan_graph/index.json is the required canonical graph entrypoint with schema version, node shard listing and hashes, entrypoints, deterministic execution ordering, validation targets, Executor Protocol status semantics, and canonical dependency semantics driven by blockers[].

items.impact: Centralizes readiness authority in blocker semantics and binds the index to shard hashes and validation targets.
items.statement: The canonical index binds graph identity, shards, deterministic ordering, validation targets, lifecycle semantics, and blocker-driven dependency authority.
items.title: Graph index contract defines headless authority

evidence.exact_quote: Node shards under plan_graph/nodes/<node_id>.json must conform to pm.project-plan-node.v1, include all required lifecycle, policy, evidence, dependency, decision, and readiness fields, and keep filename node_id, ProjectContract:*, acceptance[], and evidence_required.path integrity aligned.

items.impact: Makes node autonomy, evidence, dependencies, and acceptance bounds inspectable and cross-file verifiable.
items.statement: Every node shard must satisfy the canonical node schema and cross-file identity, contract, acceptance, and evidence-path invariants.
items.title: Node shards carry complete execution bounds

evidence.exact_quote: plan_graph/edges.json is optional and, if present, must be consistent with shard dependency semantics.

items.impact: Prevents the convenience edge projection from becoming a competing readiness authority.
items.statement: edges.json is an optional consistency projection and cannot override shard-local dependency truth.
items.title: Edges projection is non-authoritative

evidence.exact_quote: plan_graph/exports/plan_graph.monolithic.json may exist only as a faithful, lossless, noncanonical derived export.

items.impact: Allows portable export without weakening sharded canonical authority.
items.statement: A monolithic graph is permitted only as a faithful and lossless projection of the canonical sharded graph.
items.title: Monolithic graph remains a lossless export

evidence.exact_quote: Project Plan Package artifacts are canonical in seglog, with filesystem as regenerable export/cache and required artifact-event fields sufficient for hash-verified reconstruction.

items.impact: Supplies durable identity, payload, hash, timestamp, and correlation data for reconstruction and support diagnostics.
items.statement: Seglog artifact events carry the fields required to reconstruct and hash-verify filesystem materializations.
items.title: Artifact events support verified reconstruction

evidence.exact_quote: The canonical artifact_type registry maps Project Plan Package artifact types to their required, optional, GUI, validation, traceability, and quickstart logical paths.

items.impact: Prevents feature-local artifact type names and path mappings from fragmenting persistence and export behavior.
items.statement: The artifact-type registry canonically maps each package family to its logical path and required, optional, GUI, or compatibility status.
items.title: Artifact type registry owns path mappings

evidence.exact_quote: Validators must prove sharded graph validity, shard hashes, contract references, acceptance coverage, seglog hash matching, headless orchestration, and optional monolithic export consistency.

items.impact: Provides a multi-layer falsifiable gate from graph structure through canonical persistence and GUI-independent execution.
items.statement: Validators must prove graph, contract, acceptance, persistence, headless execution, and derived-export consistency rather than schema shape alone.
items.title: Validator gate covers end-to-end graph integrity

evidence.exact_quote: validate post-loop corrected artifacts until certified or critically blocked;

items.impact: Consumers may treat partially repaired bytes as certified, discard useful preserved work, or show a clean package despite a critical blocked disposition.
items.statement: The loop terminates as certified or critically blocked, but this unit does not define the atomic publication, rollback, preservation, or user-visible trust state of post-loop artifacts in the critically blocked branch.
items.title: Critical-block artifact disposition is unclear

evidence.exact_quote: Validators must enforce requirements quality and coverage JSON integrity, Markdown/JSON ID parity, and optional quickstart command, count, and size constraints.

items.impact: Makes human-readable projections and quickstart convenience output mechanically subordinate to machine-readable canon and bounded in size.
items.statement: Traceability JSON, Markdown parity, and quickstart membership and size constraints have explicit validator obligations.
items.title: Traceability and quickstart outputs are validator-bound

evidence.exact_quote: Auditor cycle reports remain upstream artifacts but must bridge backward to planning/wizard state and forward to launched execution through explicit lineage and runtime/account identity fields. The legacy `validation_pass_report` artifact family name is a compatibility mirror, not a fixed validation-pass model selector; plans-to-code audit, verification, certification, quality gates, and evidence review route to Auditor Model, and broad artifact-family rename remains deferred.

items.impact: History, export, and handoff consumers may disagree about whether a report with absent optional wizard, thread, account, or launched-run fields is complete enough for the claimed bridge.
items.statement: Backward and forward lineage are required, but the unit does not define which optional identity fields become mandatory for each origin and handoff scenario or the failure state when a bridge cannot be resolved.
items.title: Lineage bridge completeness is scenario-ambiguous

evidence.exact_quote: Traceability outputs are derived, noncanonical for planning decisions, and canonical for verification outputs.

items.impact: Stops coverage reports from changing plan intent while allowing them to be authoritative evidence of verification results.
items.statement: Traceability artifacts have explicit dual authority: derived for planning and canonical for verification outcomes.
items.title: Traceability authority is purpose-specific

segments.summary: Established the Project Plan Package scope, seglog authority, staging tree, GUI pair trigger, and the boundary from Runtime Artifacts.
Reviewed generated-media durability, provenance, expiry and secret exclusions together with package, schema, graph, and seglog continuation contracts.
Reviewed validator, lineage, traceability, quickstart, replay, and SSOT behavior; identified missing deterministic replay conflict and recovery semantics.
Reviewed runtime/package separation, identity and navigation, export trust, persistence, required outputs, and GUI pair behavior; found the identity-open resolver state machine under-specified.

Reviewed sidecar boundaries, Document Set packaging, schema and contract layers, DRY references, and autonomous decision logging; found packaging atomicity and unattended approval transitions unspecified.
Reviewed canonical sharded roots, locked entrypoints, node identity, index and shard contracts, and derived graph projections; found the node-intent canonicalization algorithm missing.

Reviewed artifact-event fields, type registry, validators, sweep finality, traceability, lineage, and verification authority; found critical-block disposition and conditional lineage completeness ambiguous.
